findings.title: [P1] Pass branch names as arguments instead of interpolating them
findings.body: When `branch` can contain shell syntax, `exec` evaluates it through a shell rather than passing it as one Git argument. For example, a value containing `;` can run an additional command with the Node process's privileges. Keep argument separation (such as the previous `execFile("git", ["show", branch])`) so branch input cannot become executable shell syntax.

findings.title: [P2] Keep Git as the directly killable child process
findings.body: Callers receive the `ChildProcess` returned by `showBranch`; after this change it represents a shell rather than Git. If a caller cancels a long-running operation with `.kill()`, the shell may terminate while its Git child continues running and retaining the output pipes. Invoking Git directly preserves the previous cancellation and process-ownership behavior.
